No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result NAJUC Writes AGF, CJ, DSS DG, IGP, NUJ, Seeks Protection From Sowore, Supporters Over Attacks by Olakunle Olasanmi 11 seconds ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The National Association of Judiciary Correspondents (NAJUC) has called for protection over incessant attacks by Omoyele Sowore, the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), and his supporters on members of the association.
NAJUC is the umbrella body of journalists covering the courts and the entire judiciary.
Sowore is standing trial before Justice Mohammed Umar of the Federal High Court in Abuja over allegations of cyberbullying.
He was said to have called President Bola Tinubu a criminal.
He is being tried before the court by the Department of State Services (DSS).
The association has written a petition to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court and the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS) over attacks on its members.
Also copied on the petition dated November 13, 2026, are the Inspector-General of Police, the National President of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) and the Chairman of NUJ, Federal Capital Territory Chapter.
NAJUC members, through their chairman, Olakunle Olasanmi, chronicled in the petition a series of attacks the association had suffered at the hands of Sowore and his supporters whenever his case comes up before the court.
According to Olasanmi, members of the association found it difficult to do their jobs whenever Sowore’s case comes up before the court.
The petition was titled, “Complaints of Attacks, Threats and Intimidation Against Journalists Covering the Federal High Court, Abuja, by Omoyele Sowore, Sydney Godwin and Their Supporters.”
The journalists, in the letter, cried out to the heads of all the agencies for help, saying their lives were no longer safe while performing their lawful duties.
“We write to bring to your notice the several attacks on our members covering the Federal High Court, Abuja, by the Presidential Candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, one Sydney Godwin and their supporters.
“Sir, each time this case comes up in court, supporters of Sowore, who besiege the court in their hundreds, intimidate and harass everyone, including our members who go about their lawful duties in the court.
“Specifically, on November 11, 2026, our members were harassed, intimidated and their property destroyed by supporters of Omoyele Sowore.
“On that same day, some of our members recounted their ordeals at the hands of Sowore’s supporters.
“The chairman of the association, Olakunle Olasanmi, had the windscreen of his car smashed at the entrance gate of the court.
“The windscreen of the car, a Toyota Venza, was shattered by Sowore’s supporters, who have always been notorious for unruly behaviour each time the criminal case filed against him by the Department of State Services comes up before the court.
“Sir, as journalists covering the court, we are finding it extremely difficult to do our jobs as we receive one attack or another either from Omoyele Sowore or his supporters each time the case comes up.
“We are, therefore, seeking protection from Sowore and his supporters to be able to do our jobs without fear of molestation and intimidation by anybody.
“As it stands, sir, our lives and property are no longer safe because of fear of attacks, threats and intimidation from Sowore and his men.
